data.title: Rubico Announces Record Date of Monday, September 28 and Ex-Dividend Date of Tuesday, October 6 for Previously-Announced 0.50 Common Shares Per Common Share Stock Dividend
data.description:
ATHENS, Greece, Sept. 25, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Rubico Inc. (“Rubico,” or the “Company”), a global provider of shipping transportation services specializing in the ownership of vessels, announces that, in relation to the previously announced stock dividend of 0.50 common shares for each common share outstanding (the “Stock Dividend”), the Nasdaq Capital Market (“Nasdaq”) has determined that the ex-dividend date will be October 6, 2026. The Stock Dividend will be distributed on or about October 5, 2026 (the “Distribution Date”) to shareholders of record as of the close of business on September 28, 2026. No fractional shares will be issued in connection with the Stock Dividend; any fractional shares resulting from the Stock Dividend will be paid in cash based on the closing price of the Company’s common shares on Nasdaq on September 28, 2026.

As a result of “due bill” trading procedures expected to be established by Nasdaq, Rubico common shares are expected to trade with due bills from September 28, 2026 through and including the Distribution Date. Accordingly, holders of Rubico common shares as of September 28, 2026 will need to hold such shares through and including the Distribution Date in order to receive the Stock Dividend.

This would mean that holders who purchase Rubico common shares during the due bill period (even if the trades are to be settled after the due bill period) will be entitled to receive the Stock Dividend with respect to those shares. Conversely, sellers who sell Rubico common shares during the due bill period (even if the trades are to be settled after the due bill period) will not be entitled to the Stock Dividend with respect to those shares.

Due bills obligate a seller of securities to deliver the distribution payable on such securities to the buyer. The due bill obligations are customarily settled between the brokers representing buyers and sellers of the securities. The Company has no obligation for either the amount of the due bill or the processing of the due bill. Buyers and sellers of Rubico’s common shares should consult their brokers before trading to ensure they understand the effect of Nasdaq’s due bill procedures.

About the Company

Rubico Inc. is a global provider of shipping transportation services specializing in the ownership of vessels. The Company is an international owner and operator of two modern, fuel efficient, eco 157,000 dwt Suezmax tankers. Furthermore, the Company owns two 47,499 dwt MR tanker newbuildings scheduled for delivery in the third and fourth quarters of 2029 and a 60-meter newbuilding megayacht scheduled for delivery in the second quarter of 2027, which the Company intends to divest. In addition, the Company has entered into a share purchase agreement to acquire a shipowning company that owns one high-specification 47,499 dwt MR tanker newbuilding scheduled for delivery in the second quarter of 2029, with closing of this share purchase agreement to occur by September 30, 2026.

The Company is incorporated under the laws of the Republic of the Marshall Islands and has executive offices in Athens, Greece. The Company’s common shares trade on the Nasdaq Capital Market under the symbol “RUBI”.

data.title: Enad Global 7 announces staff reduction at Cold Iron Studios
data.description:
Enad Global 7 (“EG7”) announces that its wholly owned subsidiary Daybreak Game Company will reduce staffing levels at Cold Iron Studios following the release of Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2.

The staff reduction follows the original plan that is intended to reduce the studio’s operating cost base and secure a sustainable operation going forward.

Following the staff reduction, Cold Iron Studios will remain focused on the continued development and support of Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2, including the Nintendo Switch 2 release that is now scheduled for early 2027.

Cold Iron Studios will continue to operate as part of Daybreak Game Company.

FOR MORE INFORMATION, PLEASE CONTACT:

Fredrik Rüdén, Group Deputy CEO and CFO

fredrik.ruden@enadglobal7.com

Phone: +46 730 587 608

robin.lundell@enadglobal7.com

About EG7

EG7 is a group of companies within the gaming industry that develops, markets, publishes and distributes PC, console and mobile games to the global gaming market. The company develops its own original IPs through its game development divisions Daybreak Games, Piranha Games and Big Blue Bubble. In addition, the Group's marketing agency Petrol has contributed to the release of 2,000+ titles, of which many are world famous brands such as Call of Duty, Destiny, and Elden Ring. The Group's publishing and distribution arm Fireshine Games hold expertise in both physical and digital publishing. EG7 is headquartered in Stockholm with approximately 535 employees in 12 offices worldwide.

data.title: Canopy Growth Announces Adjournment of 2026 Annual General and Special Meeting Due to Lack of Quorum
data.description:
Canopy Growth Corporation (“Canopy Growth”, “our”, “we” or the “Company”) (TSX: WEED) (Nasdaq: CGC), a leading global company committed to bettering lives through cannabis, today announced that, due to the requisite quorum not being present, its Annual General and Special Meeting of shareholders (the “Meeting”), scheduled for Friday, September 25, 2026, at 1:00 p.m. ET via live webcast, was convened and then adjourned.

The Meeting will reconvene on Friday, October 23, 2026, at 1:00 p.m. ET via live audio webcast at www.virtualshareholdermeeting.com/WEED2026, providing holders (“Shareholders”) of Canopy Growth common shares (the “Shares”) with additional time to vote.

During the adjournment period, the Company will continue to solicit votes with respect to the proposals set out in its definitive proxy statement dated August 7, 2026 (the “Proxy Statement”). Shareholders who have not yet voted are encouraged to do so as soon as possible.

Shareholders of record as of close of business on July 31, 2026, remain eligible to vote at the adjourned Meeting. Shareholders who have already voted do not need to vote again, and previously submitted proxies will remain valid.

Your Vote is Important

Under Nasdaq listing rules and the Company’s By-Laws, 33 1/3% of outstanding Shares entitled to vote must be present in person, by remote communication or by proxy at the Meeting for quorum to be achieved.

Shareholders who have not yet voted are encouraged to submit their vote before the new proxy voting deadline of 9:00 a.m. ET on October 23, 2026.

Most Shareholders who received a 16-digit control number from Broadridge Financial Solutions can vote:

Online: http://proxyvote.com

By Phone: 1-800-474-7493 (English) or 1-800-474-7501 (French)

By Mail: Using the prepaid envelope accompanying the Form of Proxy or Voting Instruction Form

Many Shareholders can also vote by contacting the Company’s proxy solicitation agent, Sodali & Co., at 1-833-830-8205 toll free in North America, 1-289-695-3075 collect outside North America, or by email at CGC@investor.sodali.com.

Shareholders who hold Shares at Interactive Brokers LLC can vote online at: http://proxypush.com using the provided control number.

Clients of Robinhood Securities, LLC who are eligible to vote will receive a voting notice by email from noreply@robinhood.com. Voting is hosted by Say Technologies, with voting and materials available directly from the email.

The Proxy Statement and the Company’s 2026 fiscal annual report, which includes the Company’s 2026 fiscal year consolidated financial statements (collectively, the “Meeting Materials”) are filed on EDGAR at www.sec.gov and SEDAR+ under the Company’s profile at www.sedarplus.ca. data.title: SoftBank Drops 3.2% as OpenAI Financing Locks In 9.41%
data.description:
SoftBank Group (SOBKY), the Japanese technology investor, locked in $10 billion of dollar bonds and 1 billion of euro bonds to help fund its final OpenAI investment payment. Shares fell 3.18% to 6,150 at Friday's 3:30 p.m. Tokyo close. The financing is in place. Now the returns have to justify its cost.

SoftBank's dollar bonds carry rates of 8.625%, 9.25% and 9.75%. On the amounts issued, that adds up to about $941 million in annual interest; the euro bonds add roughly 75.6 million. The company expects to issue the notes on September 29 and close the $10 billion OpenAI payment on October 1. Reuters called the transaction the largest high-yield corporate bond sale on record, citing LSEG data.

The picture gives investors a useful tension to watch: SoftBank's GF Score is 79 out of 100, but financial strength and momentum sit below profitability. A strong investment record can help make the OpenAI bet; it cannot erase the interest bill. SoftBank needs the value of that stake to grow enough to reward shareholders after the cost of borrowing.

data.title: Dell Stock Jumps 3.5% as Gemini Enters the XPS Franchise
data.description:
Dell Technologies , the maker of PCs and AI infrastructure, introduced a $999 XPS Googlebook built around Gemini Intelligence and Android phone integration. Shares rose about 3.5% to $555.32 at 10.42am ET time on Friday, September 25. The question for investors is whether Dell can turn those software features into premium laptop sales.

The 13-inch machine pairs a Snapdragon X Elite chip with a 2.5K touchscreen and up to 32GB of memory. Dell says it can stream video for up to 16 hours and will reach Dell.com in October. Dell is entering a crowded field: Reuters reported that four other PC makers are joining Google's new laptop category, with entry prices starting at $899.

The valuation leaves little room for a launch that merely looks good. At $555.32, Dell's share price stood 139.62% above the $231.75 GF Value shown for September 25. That gap is a reason to watch margins and sales, not to assume one new laptop will move earnings. Dell's AI infrastructure business remains the bigger financial driver; the XPS Googlebook still has to prove customers will pay its premium price.

data.title: Arm Stocks Surge as Muse Makes CPUs Matter Again
data.description:
Arm Holdings , the chip architecture and data center processor company, rose about 4.2% to $319.18 at 10.40am ET time on Friday, September 25, as investors continued to weigh what AI agents could mean for CPU demand. Barron's linked this week's enthusiasm for Arm and other chip stocks to interest in Meta's Muse agent.

The idea is straightforward: an agent working through a long task needs processors to run applications, coordinate steps and move data, even when AI accelerators handle the model itself. Arm has a product pitch for that work. The company introduced its AGI CPU alongside Neoverse CSS N4, a platform that supports up to 128 cores per die. More agent activity could mean more CPU demand; how much of that spending reaches Arm is still an open question.

There is already a lot of optimism in the share price. At $319.18, Arm traded 64.21% above its $194.37 GF Value estimate. That gap puts pressure on the company to turn interest in agent infrastructure into chip shipments and revenue, rather than leave investors paying today for demand that may take years to arrive.

data.title: Qualcomm Stocks Jump as Apple Extends the Royalty Bridge
data.description:
Qualcomm , the wireless-chip and edge-AI company, renewed its global patent license with Apple, effective April 1, 2027. Shares rose about 2.4% to $198.95 at 10.37am ET Time on Friday, September 25. Apple is building more of its own modems, but that shift does not end its patent relationship with Qualcomm.

The distinction matters for revenue. Patent royalties and modem sales are separate businesses. Reuters reported that licensing accounted for roughly 15% of Qualcomm's June-quarter revenue, even as the company expects Apple-related chip sales to decline in 2027. Qualcomm disclosed neither the new license's end date nor its financial terms.

Qualcomm is pushing beyond phones, too: it says more than 13,000 businesses have deployed or tested Snapdragon-powered PCs. Yet the shares trade 13.46% above their $175.35 GF Value. The Apple renewal protects an important royalty stream; investors are also paying for Qualcomm to turn its expansion into lasting growth.

data.title: Micron Stock Gets Another Vote of Confidence From Top Analyst
data.description:
Micron Technology (MU) received a bullish note from Rosenblatt Securities ahead of its September 30 earnings report, with senior research analyst Kevin Cassidy maintaining a Buy rating and a $1,500 price target.

Cassidy said Micron could benefit from additional strategic customer agreements, firmer memory pricing and potentially higher share repurchases in fiscal 2027. He also argued that investor concerns about rising wafer capacity may be weighing on the stock despite continued demand from artificial intelligence applications.

Micron has signed 16 strategic customer agreements covering about 20% of its DRAM output and roughly one-third of its NAND production. Cassidy said such agreements could eventually provide coverage for as much as 40% of output over three to five years while improving demand visibility.

Rosenblatt expects average selling prices for DRAM and NAND to rise 10% sequentially in the November quarter. The firm models $56.5 billion in revenue and an 86% gross margin, with stronger pricing offering additional upside.

Micron's share repurchase restrictions are also expected to expire in December, potentially.

data.title: Libra Announces Strategic Institutional Financing Led by SIDEX and NQ Mining Investment
data.description:
Toronto, Ontario--(Newsfile Corp. - September 25, 2026) - Libra Energy Materials Inc. (OTCQB: LIBRF) (FSE: W0R0) ("Libra" or the "Company") is pleased to announce a strategic private placement of CMETC flow-through common shares ("CMETC Shares") for aggregate gross proceeds of $725,000 (the "Offering"). The Offering is led by Québec-based institutional investors SIDEX limited partnership ("SIDEX") and NQ Mining Investment ("NQMI").

The Offering will consist of 5,000,000 CMETC Shares at a price of $0.145 per CMETC Share. The CMETC Shares issued under the Offering will be subject to a statutory hold period of four months and one day from the closing date. A finder's fee will be payable in cash to certain arm's length finders engaged in connection with the Offering, subject to the approval of the CSE.

The gross proceeds will be used to incur "Canadian exploration expenses" that qualify as "flow-through mining expenditures" under the Income Tax Act (Canada) on the Company's Québec projects, including the newly acquired flagship projects Cisco West and Obamska in the Eeyou Istchee James Bay region. The Company will renounce these expenditures to subscribers with an effective date no later than December 31, 2026. The CMETC FT Shares will also qualify for the Canadian government's Critical Mineral Exploration Tax Credit.

Closing of the Offering is expected on or about September 29, 2026, and remains subject to customary closing conditions, including receipt of all necessary regulatory approvals of the Canadian Securities Exchange (the "CSE"). No insiders are expected to participate in the Offering.

data.title: MARINE PETROLEUM TRUST FY 2026: Revenue $985.7K, Net income $659.8K — 10-K Summary
data.description:
MARINE PETROLEUM TRUST reported distributable income of $659781 for fiscal 2026 on revenue of $985720 declines of 9.4% and 5.6% respectively from fiscal 2025, according to its 10-K summary.

Financial Highlights

  • Revenue was $985.7K for FY2026, compared with $1,043.8K in FY2025; YoY change (5.6%).
  • Net income (distributable income) was $659.8K for FY2026, compared with $728.0K in FY2025; YoY change (9.4%).
  • Diluted earnings per share: Not reported in the filing and therefore omitted.

Business Highlights

  • Distributable income fell to $659,781 in FY2026 from $727,995 in FY2025, driven by lower oil and NGL prices and reduced volumes.
  • Production mix: Oil volumes rose to 14,076 barrels in FY2026 while natural gas and NGL volumes declined; the trust reported 69 net active wells.
  • Prices: Average oil price dropped to $63.88 per barrel; natural gas averaged $3.56 per mcf. Royalties were received net of transportation costs.
  • Operational limits: The trust is prohibited from operating businesses or replacing depleting assets, making income dependent on third‑party production and market prices.
  • Distributions and liquidity: Quarterly distributions remained at $0.10 per unit, funded from available cash with reserves held for estimated expenses.

Original SEC Filing: MARINE PETROLEUM TRUST [ MARPS ] - 10-K - Sep. 25, 2026

data.title: Golden Spike Announces Effective Date of Share Consolidation and Name Change to Gordon Mining Group Inc.
data.description:
Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - September 25, 2026) - Golden Spike Resources Corp. (OTCQB: GSPRF) (FSE: L5Y) ("Golden Spike" or the "Company") is pleased to announce that further to its news release on August 17, 2026, the Company will proceed to change its name to "Gordon Mining Group Inc." (the "Name Change") and consolidate the Company's issued and outstanding common shares (the "Shares") on the basis of one (1) post-consolidation Share for every five (5) pre-consolidation Shares (the "Consolidation").

The Shares are expected to begin trading on the Canadian Securities Exchange under the ticker symbol "GORD" at the opening of trading on September 30, 2026. The new CUSIP for the Shares is 38277A103 and the new ISIN is CA38277A1030.

Immediately prior to the Consolidation, the Company had 60,566,666 Shares issued and outstanding. Following completion of the Consolidation, the Company is expected to have approximately 12,113,333 Shares issued and outstanding, subject to adjustments for rounding. No fractional Shares will be issued in connection with the Consolidation. Any fractional interest resulting from the Consolidation will be rounded down to the nearest whole Share.

The exercise price of the Company's existing stock options under the Company's stock option plan, the number of Shares issuable thereunder, and the exercise price and number of Shares issuable under any outstanding warrants of the Company will be adjusted in accordance with the Consolidation. Following the Consolidation, approximately 1,055,000 Shares will be reserved for issuance upon the exercise of outstanding stock options and approximately 6,432,563 Shares will be reserved for issuance upon the exercise of outstanding warrants.

The Board of Directors believes that the Name Change and Consolidation will better align the Company's identity with its strategic objectives and provide greater flexibility to pursue future financing, business development and acquisition opportunities. The Board also believes that the Consolidation may broaden the Company's appeal to investors and support long-term shareholder value. Under the Company's Articles, the Name Change and Consolidation required only Board approval.

data.title: SK Hynix’s U.S.-Based Solidigm Unit Reportedly Weighs IPO – Offering Expected Next Year At A Valuation Near $150B
data.description:
Key points:
  • Solidigm was created after SK Hynix acquired Intel Corp.’s NAND flash memory and storage operations.
  • SK Hynix paid $8.8 billion for Solidigm, completing the acquisition in March 2025.
  • Solidigm targets data-center and AI storage workloads with enterprise solid-state drives offering capacities of up to 122.88 terabytes.

SK Hynix Inc. (SKHY) is reportedly considering an initial public offering (IPO) of its U.S.-based Solidigm unit as early as next year. The issue could value the storage-chip business at up to $150 billion, Reuters reported Friday, citing people familiar with the matter.

Solidigm could raise about $15 billion through the offering. According to the report, at the top end of the potential valuation range, the listing would rank among the largest semiconductor IPOs on record, giving the NAND and enterprise storage business a standalone public-market valuation.

The potential deal remains at an early stage, and its size and timing could change depending on market conditions, Reuters reported.

What Does Solidigm Do?

Solidigm was created after SK Hynix (SKHY) acquired Intel Corp.’s (INTC) NAND flash memory and storage operations. SK Hynix’s U.S. prospectus showed that it paid $6.6 billion in December 2021 and another $2.2 billion in March 2025 to complete the $8.8 billion transaction.

The South Korean memory giant established Solidigm as a U.S. subsidiary to operate the acquired business. The company focuses on NAND flash memory solutions, particularly high-end enterprise solid-state drives (SSDs), using technologies including quad-level cell NAND.

Solidigm markets its D5-P5336 data-center solid-state drive (SSD) with capacities of up to 122.88 terabytes. In practical terms, the high-capacity drive lets data centers store large amounts of information on fewer drives, making it well-suited to AI, machine learning, and other workloads that require companies to process and retain enormous datasets.

Could Be The Largest Semiconductor Listing Ever

A valuation of up to $150 billion would put Solidigm well above several recent semiconductor IPOs. Arm Holdings debuted in 2023 at a valuation of about $54 billion, while Cerebras Systems entered the public market in 2026 at a fully diluted valuation of roughly $56 billion.

The broader NAND market puts Solidigm and SK Hynix against Samsung Electronics, Kioxia, Micron Technology Inc. (MU) and SanDisk Corp. (SNDK), which SK Hynix identifies as its major NAND competitors.

A Bigger US Footprint?

The IPO deliberations come as Solidigm also considers expanding its manufacturing footprint in the U.S.

Reuters reported last week that the company is weighing a U.S. NAND flash memory factory, with upstate New York among the potential locations. Such a plant could reduce its reliance on its existing manufacturing operation in Dalian, China, although SK Hynix said it had not confirmed any specific plan.

A potential Solidigm listing would also follow SK Hynix’s own U.S. market debut earlier this year. The key next step is whether SK Hynix moves from considering a Solidigm listing to formally pursuing an offering, including determining the size, timing and valuation.

data.title: Man charged in $16 million crypto ‘massive pig butchering’ scam
data.description:
The U.S. Attorney's Office in Missouri charged a man on Friday for his role in defrauding someone of millions of dollars' worth of crypto in a "massive pig butchering" scam.

The attorney's office said in a statement that Trung Nguyen Van, 37, from Vietnam, was charged with money laundering for his role. Pig butchering scams, also known as romance scams, build relationships with users and then lure them into fraudulent investments.

"Pig butchering schemes are an increasingly prevalent and sophisticated form of fraud that have caused billions of dollars in losses to victims around the world," said R. Matthew Price, U.S. Attorney for the Western District of Missouri, in a statement.

Prosecutors said that during the summer of 2024, the victim transferred about $16 million worth of crypto because they thought they were investing in a crypto platform called "Triangle." Right after receiving the funds, Van allegedly transferred them into private crypto wallets.

Other victims may have been involved as well. Other U.S. based victims have reported millions of dollars in losses and attributed those to wallets that sent funds to Van's crypto wallet, prosecutors said.

"Each of the victims were instructed to transfer cryptocurrency to different websites, but each victim reported a similar story," the attorney's office said. "In each of these schemes, victims were guided by an individual they met online to invest cryptocurrency in a specified 'website' with a promise of high financial returns."

data.title: U.S. Appeals Court Upholds Pentagon Labeling Anthropic a Security Risk — WSJ
data.description:
By Amrith Ramkumar and Heather Somerville

WASHINGTON-A federal appeals court upheld the Defense Department's decision to designate Anthropic a security risk, giving the Trump administration a win in its complicated feud with one of the nation's top artificial-intelligence developers.

The federal appeals court in Washington said in a 2-1 decision Friday that the law giving the Pentagon the authority to deem a company a supply-chain risk gave Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth the latitude to take the action against Anthropic because the company's refusal to have its AI tools used in mass surveillance or autonomous weapons could undermine military operations.

"The Department had ample support for its conclusion that the continued integration of Claude into the Department's information systems, by the Department or its contractors, presented a statutorily covered national-security risk," the court wrote. Anthropic had argued that the designation was an unprecedented attack retaliating against the company for disagreeing with the Defense Department in contract negotiations. A federal judge in California recently sided with the company in a parallel dispute covering parts of the designation under a different statute, fueling uncertainty about the future of the supply-chain risk label.

Legal analysts have said that a split between the courts could ultimately lead to the Supreme Court.

"We respectfully disagree with the court's decision. Another federal court has already held the government's parallel designation unlawful. We remain confident in our position and are considering all options, including further review," an Anthropic spokeswoman said.

The supply-chain risk is normally used on companies based in foreign adversaries like China's Huawei who pose security risks. AI analysts have said the administration's move was a self-inflicted wound in the global AI race because it could damage Anthropic, which makes some of the nation's most powerful models and has said it has lost contracts and suffered reputational harm from the move.

A win for the government could give the Pentagon more latitude to take similar actions against companies in the future, analysts have said.

The rulings are part of a delicate relationship between the Trump administration and Anthropic, which are working together on the release of new AI models while the legal fight continues. The company has vaulted ahead in the AI race by many measures and is barreling toward an initial public offering in which it is aiming for a valuation of about $2 trillion.

Pentagon officials have said the department is nearly entirely done moving away from Anthropic's models using tools from OpenAI and other competitors.

At a hearing at the federal appeals court earlier this year, the three-judge panel appeared split, with two of the judges seeming sympathetic to the administration's argument that it had the authority to use the supply-chain risk designation regardless of the guardrails Anthropic was pursuing in their negotiations.

"It's about risk, and they say, 'Well, based on what we know, we can't trust that the [AI] model may not have something embedded within it that is going to create a problem for military capabilities," said Neomi Rao, a judge appointed during the first Trump administration.

Judge Karen LeCraft Henderson, who was appointed by former President George H.W. Bush, disagreed and published a dissenting opinion Thursday. "To me this is just a spectacular overreach by the department," she said during the hearing.

Write to Amrith Ramkumar at amrith.ramkumar@wsj.com and Heather Somerville at heather.somerville@wsj.com

data.title: Edelweiss Financial Services sells 45% Nido Home Finance stake to Carlyle for ₹600 crore
data.description:
Edelweiss Financial Services Ltd on Friday (September 25) announced the completion of Carlyle’s investment of over ₹2,000 crore in Nido Home Finance Ltd, giving the global investment firm’s affiliated funds a strategic majority stake in the housing finance company.

The investment funds affiliated with Carlyle Asia Partners (CAP), part of The Carlyle Group, have invested approximately ₹2,000 crore, or about $215 million, in Nido through a combination of primary capital infusion and secondary purchase.

The primary capital infusion is approximately ₹1,450 crore, of which around ₹725 crore has been received. The balance is to be received within 18 months. Following the primary infusion, Nido’s net worth is set to nearly triple to approximately ₹2,300 crore within 18 months.

Carlyle has also completed the secondary purchase of a 45% stake in Nido from Edelweiss for approximately ₹600 crore. Edelweiss will hold approximately 26% of Nido on a fully diluted basis at the end of 18 months.

Edelweiss will also receive a share of the upside if Carlyle realises returns above a specified threshold. The transaction was announced on February 10, 2026, and has been completed following receipt of the requisite regulatory and statutory approvals.

Nido, established in 2010, is a housing finance company offering home loan solutions across the affordable housing and mid-ticket market segments. Its branch network serves more than 800 talukas, or sub-districts, and it had assets under management of ₹4,900 crore as of the quarter ended June 2026.

For Edelweiss, the transaction provides Nido with fresh growth capital, while allowing Edelweiss to monetise part of its stake and reduce debt. Nido will also have access to Carlyle’s operating expertise.

The company said the primary equity infusion is expected to strengthen Nido’s financial foundation and position it to serve affordable and mid-ticket housing segments across rural, semi-urban and emerging markets.

Edelweiss operates seven independent businesses spanning alternative asset management, mutual funds, asset reconstruction, non-banking finance, housing finance, general insurance and life insurance. It employs more than 6,000 people, serves around 1.4 crore customers and manages around ₹2,80,000 crore of assets.

Shares of Edelweiss Financial Services Ltd ended at ₹137.20, down by ₹1.85, or 1.33%, on the BSE.

data.title: 'Lift Your Game': Former Australian PM Kevin Rudd Addresses OpenAI CEO Over Portal Breach — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Andy Serwer

Kevin Rudd, the former prime minister of Australia, has something to say to OpenAI CEO Sam Altman-and the rest of Silicon Valley.

"Lift your game, Sam," Rudd said Thursday in an interview with me at Journal House, which was held on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York.

Rudd was speaking about an incident this summer in which an OpenAI agent infiltrated a government-services website in Australia. The breach was disclosed by Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese on Wednesday at the United Nations meeting in New York.

"I'm just being very blunt about it," said Rudd. "There's sometimes a bit of a cavalier culture out there in [Silicon] Valley about these things. We're a sovereign state. We take our cyber defenses seriously. We're a modern democracy. We have an excellent collaborative relationship with the major AI companies and the platform providers, but it does depend on them notifying us when a problem arises."

The Wall Street Journal reported that that the OpenAI incident appears to be the first publicly disclosed occurence of an artificial-intelligence agent gaining unauthorized access to a government service. Albanese said the incident began June 18, and that the agent gained access to both public and nonpublic files in the country's public-facing healthcare statistics portal, which reports spending and other information.

OpenAI confirmed the incident, with a spokesperson telling The Journal, "In the course of that, our models took actions we did not intend."

The incident occurred in June, but OpenAI did not discover it until August and reported it to the Australians on Sept. 10th, the Journal reported. Rudd, the former ambassador to the United States and current CEO of the educational non-profit Asia Society, thinks OpenAI did a poor job of notifying the Australian government about the problem.

"OpenAI apparently had their own internal awareness of this some time ago, but there was a huge delay in their formal notification of the Australian government," he said. "OpenAI is saying they sent some obscure email to some obscure inbox somewhere. The bottom line is, if you've got an AI agent, which you know as the originating company has breached cyber defenses of the social or economic infrastructure of one of your partner countries in a large market, then you should be on the telephone immediately, so that the appropriate agencies, in our case the Australian Signals Directorate, can automatically act on cyber defenses through our own cyber command."

OpenAI did not immediately respond to Barron's request for comment.

I asked Rudd what sort of damage the breach caused.

"I'm sure the [Prime Minister] will outline later to the Australian people what, if anything, was compromised," Rudd said. "Now, I'm not in that loop-I've now left government service about three months ago. But we take these things step by step."

"Look, mistakes happen," he added. "We understand that nothing in the world is perfect, but given how fast this game is moving in terms of frontier models, not withstanding what [Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei] had to say the other day, this now needs to be a much smoother operation than is currently the case in terms of the intersection between the frontier model-has it been tested against cyber defenses before its release? If not-and even if so, and if a breach occurs, to immediately get on the phone to say, 'Houston, we have a problem,' or 'Sydney, we have a problem.'"

Write to Andy Serwer at andy.serwer@barrons.com

data.title: What's Moving Markets Today? — WSJ
data.description:
By Shradha Dinesh

Major stock indexes ticked up on Friday following a dizzying news week spanning record high yields on Treasurys, seesawing updates on the state of negotiations with Iran, a Chinese state visit and more.

Here's what is moving markets today:

Oil prices: After remaining quiet for much of the morning, Brent crude extended declines after initial reports suggest that sideline talks between the U.S. and Iran from the U.N. assembly in New York have progressed to a "technical stage," according to Al-Jazeera. Brent crude fell about 3% to $97 a barrel.

Tech: Five of the Magnificent Seven are up. Meta Platforms and Tesla are, so far, Friday's laggards. Meta rode the wave of enthusiasm for its new personal AI agent, Muse, and followed up with its expansions into hardware Wednesday. The company unveiled a handheld keychain device that can be used to talk to Muse agents and added Muse to its more controversial smartglasses.

Diesel: The nationwide average diesel price per gallon, which hit a record-breaking $6.53 Tuesday, has ended its daily new-record streak. Prices in the back half of the week have hovered around $6.50, according to AAA. The slowdown follows a week of public back-and-forth as some candidates facing tight midterm races said they would back a diesel export ban.

data.title: Trump Calls Xi Meeting 'Very Productive.' What Investors Might Not Like. — Barrons.com
data.description:
Reshma Kapadia

President Donald Trump said in a social media post Friday he had a "very productive" meeting with Chinese leader Xi Jinping, but offered few details.

Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said in a television interview Friday that details of what the two sides reached on trade would come Monday.

While investors likely will be pleased to see signs of a fragile peace between the two economic superpowers and indications that the leaders could meet at least twice more this year, the lack of deals and a shorter-than-expected extension of the rivals' latest truce leaves plenty of uncertainty for markets in the months ahead.

In fact, the biggest takeaway for investors so far actually happened before the summit. The two countries extended their truce that was set to expire on Nov. 10 for another two months-the brief extension underscores the distrust and frictions simmering beneath the friendly tone that the leaders struck.

"I had been pretty sanguine on the U.S.-China relationship. But with an extension of only two months, that's a bit concerning," says Rory Green, head of China research for TS Lombard.

Greer told CNBC on Friday that the two sides had made fresh progress in negotiations around U.S. agricultural products, medical devices, and Chinese consumer goods deemed nonsensitive, with more information coming next week. The U.S. and China have been discussing a Board of Trade that would lower tariffs on $30 billion of nonstrategic goods, with analysts expecting many of them to be consumer-oriented.

Otherwise, the much-anticipated summit between the leaders of the world's two largest economies brought a lot of optics, but not much substance. Xi's first visit to Washington, D.C. in a decade was heavy on ceremony and goodwill-building: Trump greeted him on the tarmac in a rare move, hosted him for a state dinner, and said they have "never gotten along better." Xi has been pushing to be recognized as a global power on par with the U.S., something the visit reinforced.

Both leaders talked up their strong rapport and vowed increased cooperation and communication as they try to navigate their geopolitical rivalry. Trump and Xi are intent on preserving stability to buy each country time to reduce their dependence on the other-and to forestall a series of retaliatory measures that would make both economies' domestic problems worse.

China's economy is still stuck in a multiyear rout, with another batch of data showing weakness, even as Xi tries to project strength and equal standing with the U.S. on the global stage. Trump has his own problems, including the Iran war stretching into its seventh month and rising prices ahead of midterm elections.

The talks, however, did little to address the biggest issues among the rivals. Among them are China's support for Iran and increased military posture in Asia, the continued trade imbalance between the U.S. and China, and the two countries' race to develop artificial intelligence. Instead, the short truce extension underscores U.S. concerns about its access to rare-earth minerals and a desire to keep China to its commitments.

The U.S. is focused on getting rare-earth flows back to levels before the flare-up with China last summer, but exports are still down 25%, according to Scott Kennedy, a senior adviser at the Center for Strategic and International Studies.

That gives China some leverage: The country could clamp down on those rare earths used in everything from autos to semiconductors.

That means if the U.S.-China relationship's precarious stability wavers, investors may need to brace again for higher costs, whether they result from tariffs, shortages, or supply chain disruptions.

Brian McCarthy, managing partner at Macrolens, sees the short extension as a signal that escalation could follow, particularly because there have been few signs of progress on the administration's goal of rebalancing the relationship.

"A number of U.S. officials anticipate that the U.S.-China relationship will likely encounter some turbulent waters in the weeks after the visit, even as we expect these other leader-level meetings to continue to provide a veneer of stability," says Daniel Kritenbrink, a former diplomat and now partner at consultancy The Asia Group.

Potential irritants loom, including the Trump administration's Section 301 investigation into excess capacity that could result in tariffs of 7.5% or more against China, as well as a spate of Congressional efforts to tighten restrictions on China.

The two sides also said they would begin a dialogue over AI safety. However, there were few details and little sign that AI experts from either side were in the room-leaving investors unnerved that tensions over AI are only going to intensify.

"If U.S. tech firms agree to slow the pace of AI development domestically, it will increase calls in Washington for the U.S. to slow down China as well-such as by closing loopholes on Chinese AI firms' access to compute through the cloud," writes Michael Hirson, 22V Research's head of China research. "This raises the prospect of Chinese retaliation and is one reason why we continue to expect 2027 to see an increase in tensions around tech and supply chains."

Write to Reshma Kapadia at reshma.kapadia@barrons.com
